summary: Register-only cold review (version 14) of the concise study of the 1962 Christ the King proper: synthesis.tex and sections/concise/01-inventory, 02-overview, 03-date-location (explanatory prose), 04-themes, 10-commentary and 90-apparatus. Every reader-facing sentence was read against guidance/editorial.md 'Say what the texts say, plainly', the review.md and synthesis-review.md fragments, and the concise-study profile. Source support, chronology, pagination and manifests were not checked; other dispatches own them. Pages 1 and 2 are plain, apart from production vocabulary in the subtitle and one table-mechanics phrase. Pages 3-4 and the commentary repeat the defects the 21 October register record named in this study, and two of editorial.md's own examples are still present: 'Then the words on which the feast turns:' (04-themes.tex:72) and a variant of 'the inheritance is not territory but ...' (10-commentary.tex:53). Six recurring patterns are blocking: liturgical texts credited with the study's inferences; asserted significance and coherence; maxim and restatement closers; denials of positions nobody holds; production vocabulary ('formulary', 'elements', 'readings', 'witnesses', 'carry', 'grammar'); and refrains, with a closing paragraph that re-argues each section. Two advisories cover isolated performed emphasis and jargon in the apparatus. Quotations, and the sources' own antitheses (Augustine's in/of, Hilary's 'not his power but us', Cassiodorus's paradox, Chrysostom's servants), were not counted as defects. The repairs change sentences only; no evidence, attribution or qualification needs to be removed.

findings.problem: Liturgical texts are credited with the study's own inferences and given verbs texts do not perform (turn, move, measure, answer, set a moment, supply, name a connection, press, stand between, hold together). The pattern runs through pages 3-4 and the commentary. Instances: 04-themes.tex:9-10 'This Mass sets a throne in heaven and a prisoner in a governor's hall, and it sings of them as one King'; 04:13 'Between the two stands the sacrifice'; 04:30 'The Collect turns from the throne to the earth'; 04:52 'The two chants after the Epistle measure that kingdom' (Schuster's reading, credited first to the chants); 04:67 'Then the Gospel moves from every shore to one room'; 04:81 'Set beside the chants, the denial sharpens every claim the Mass has made'; 04:91 'The Offertory answers from the second psalm'; 04:97-98 'it sets the Son's asking at the moment of the offering'; 04:103-104 'the gifts of unity and peace: the remedy of the Collect's wound' (a cross-text link credited to the Secret); 04:116 'That handing over meets the chants that deny any end'; 10-commentary.tex:120 'Quas primas holds both titles together'; 10:270 'Quas primas holds the two halves in the same way'; 10:124 'The answer changes how the surrounding elements are heard'; 10:127 'The Epistle supplies the means and the moment of the receiving'; 10:129-130 'The Secret then names the asking that the Fathers found in the psalm'; 10:178 'The formulary keeps both of Aquinas's senses'; 10:244-245 'The Introit's verse names the measure of that office'; 10:276 'The Postcommunion presses the same question on the faithful'; 10:359-360 'The Secret shows the Priest still offering and still giving unity and peace now'; 10:362-363 'the Gospel's non est hinc names a kingdom whose origin is the Father's and whose end is the Father's too'; 10:393 'The Postcommunion stands between them'.
findings.required_result: Each text says, asks, sings, quotes, keeps or omits only what it actually does. Where a connection is a Father's, name the Father; where it is the study's own inference, state it once as an inference. Rewrites: 04:30 'The Collect turns from the throne to the earth.' -> 'The Collect prays for the peoples of the earth.' 04:97-98 'Sung as the gifts are brought to the altar, it sets the Son's asking at the moment of the offering.' -> 'The antiphon is sung while the gifts are brought to the altar.' (If the link to the offering is wanted, attribute it: 'Augustine refers the asking to the Manhood "who offered up Himself as a Sacrifice" (2.7).') 10:127-129 'The Epistle supplies the means and the moment of the receiving ...' -> 'The Epistle names redemption "through his blood", and Aquinas reads the headship of the Church as Christ's as man, secundum quod huiusmodi (Super Col. 1 lect. 5).' 10:129-130 'The Secret then names the asking that the Fathers found in the psalm.' -> 'Taken this way, the sacrifice the Secret offers is the asking Augustine finds in Ps 2:8.' 10:362-363: cut the sentence; the Gospel's 'not from hence' is already quoted and discussed at 10:144-177.

findings.problem: Significance and coherence are asserted rather than shown: the feast 'turns' on a verse, the Preface is 'the argument of the whole feast', the three interpretations 'are complementary' and 'share more than they divide'. Pages 3-4 are partly filled with such sentences, which the synthesis-review fragment calls padding. Instances: 04-themes.tex:72 'Then the words on which the feast turns:' (the exact example editorial.md gives as the defect); 04:105 'The proper Preface then gives the argument of the whole feast in one sentence'; 04:126-127 'The formulary's movement thus raises three questions, and each of three readings takes one as its own'; 10-commentary.tex:12 'The formulary can be read whole in three ways'; 10:16 'They answer different questions and are complementary'; 10:141-142 'the Mass's chants of universal dominion depend on the answer'; 10:172-173 'draws the conclusion that resolves the Mass's apparent contradiction' (no source names a contradiction in the Mass); 10:350 'The third reading draws the rest of the Mass toward that end'; 10:395 'Each reading hears the Communion in its own key'; 10:403 'The three readings share more than they divide'; 10:412 'Their four senses diverge where their questions do'; 10:434-435 'Together they say what the Preface says in one sentence:'.
findings.required_result: Where importance is a real claim, make the evidence the sentence: say what the text does and who reads it that way. Otherwise cut the sentence. Rewrites: 04:72 'Then the words on which the feast turns:' -> 'Jesus answers:'. 04:105 'The proper Preface then gives the argument of the whole feast in one sentence. The Father anointed ...' -> 'The proper Preface is a single sentence: the Father anointed ...'. 10:172-173 '... and draws the conclusion that resolves the Mass's apparent contradiction:' -> '... and concludes:'. 10:403 'The three readings share more than they divide. All identify ...' -> 'All three interpretations identify the kingdom with the redeemed people, the Church.' 10:395: cut 'Each reading hears the Communion in its own key.'; the next sentence already gives each interpretation's answer.

findings.problem: Paragraphs end, or pause, on a maxim, paradox, chiasmus or tricolon that restates the source just quoted or the paragraph just written. Deleting the sentence loses nothing. Instances: 04-themes.tex:24-25 'The Lamb is worthy because he was slain, and what he is worthy to receive includes divinity itself' (paraphrases the antiphon just quoted); 04:82-83 'The kingdom that rules from sea to sea is declared by a bound man to come from somewhere else'; 10-commentary.tex:52-53 'The Son gains nothing as God; the servant he became is raised into the glory the Word always had' (restates Hilary 2.33, just quoted); 10:57-59 'Hilary is expounding the psalm, but his words are the Epistle's'; 10:78-80 'The Son does not ask because he lacks; he asks because the Father wills that even what is owed be received as a gift, and the asking is his passion' (restates Aquinas, just quoted); 10:96-97 'The giver and the receiver are the same Son in his two natures'; 10:101-102 'He does not become what he was not'; 10:161-162 'The kingdom gathers its people by truth heard and grace given, not by the strength of servants'; 10:175-177 'A kingdom that took its origin from one place ... One whose origin is above is bounded by none, and can claim the whole earth without competing with any power in it'; 10:269 'None of the three moments makes Christ a competitor for Caesar's throne'; 10:354-356 'so that what is given to the Son is what the Son gives to the Father'; 10:435-438 'the anointed Son reigns by right, reigns as the crucified Priest, and reigns towards the Father'.
findings.required_result: End each paragraph when its information ends. Cut closers that restate; keep a sentence only if it adds a fact, a source's argument, or a step of inference stated as such. Rewrites: 10:52-53: cut 'The Son gains nothing as God; the servant he became is raised into the glory the Word always had.' The Hilary quotation that comes just before it says this. 10:78-80: cut 'The Son does not ask because he lacks; ...' or reduce it to 'For Aquinas the asking is made by prayer and by the passion.' 10:96-97 'The giver and the receiver are the same Son in his two natures.' -> cut; Bede's 'a Patre et a seipso, secundum id quod Deus est' already states it. 04:24-25 -> cut, or keep only the fact the quotation does not give: 'The antiphon's word is divinitatem.' 10:354-356 '... the reading puts the two together, so that what is given ...' -> 'Taken together, the two passages identify the nations given to the Son in Ps 2:8 with the kingdom he delivers in 1 Cor 15:24.'

findings.problem: 'Not X but Y' denials of positions that no source, text, or careful reader puts forward, including a variant of the example editorial.md names from this same study. The straw 'territory' then recurs as a refrain. Instances: 04-themes.tex:45 'The kingdom is not conquered; its subjects are carried into it'; 10-commentary.tex:53-54 'And the inheritance is not territory but the nations baptized and taught' (editorial.md's own example of the defect, still present); 10:404 'and none lets it become a territory'; 10:430-434 'Each answer would mislead on its own. The first, alone, would mislead if it let the kingship begin at Easter. The second, alone, could leave ... as ornaments ... The third, alone, could pass over ...' (hypothetical misreadings that none of the cited witnesses hold, set up only to be closed off).
findings.required_result: State Y. Keep a denial only where a named source or the text holds the X (as at 10:306-311, where Cyril answers those who say the reign stops). Rewrites: 10:53-54 -> 'The inheritance is the nations baptized and taught, carried ex iniusto ... iure dominantium ...'. 04:45 'The kingdom is not conquered; its subjects are carried into it.' -> cut it; 'translated us into the kingdom' (1:13) is already quoted. Or: 'Paul's verb is translated: the Father carries its subjects into it.' 10:404: cut ', and none lets it become a territory'. 10:430-434: cut the paragraph's three hypotheticals and keep a direct comparison, e.g. 'The first places the receiving of the kingdom in the passion and resurrection, the second places the kingdom's origin above and its people on earth, and the third places its end in the vision of God.'

findings.problem: The production's working vocabulary is used in reader prose as if the reader shared it: 'formulary', 'elements', 'reading(s)' for the study's three interpretations (this collides with the Mass's own readings, Epistle and Gospel, which the same pages discuss), 'witnesses' as a term of art, 'carry', 'grammar' and 'key' as metaphors, 'movement'. Interpretations are made grammatical subjects that 'hear', 'rest on', 'grant', 'draw' and 'put together'. Instances: synthesis.tex:21 subtitle 'three readings compared'; synthesis.tex:14 PDF subject 'the movement of the formulary ... three readings of the whole Mass'; 04-themes.tex:126-127 'The formulary's movement thus raises three questions, and each of three readings'; 10-commentary.tex:12-16 'The formulary can be read whole ... reads the Mass from ... Their witnesses divide'; 10:34-35 'their answers carry over to the Lamb'; 10:90 'St Bede brings the same grammar to the Apocalypse itself'; 10:100 'on the first reading'; 10:116 'The witnesses agree'; 10:124 'the surrounding elements'; 10:178 'The formulary keeps'; 10:185 'the first and second readings'; 10:190 'the second reading's own principal witnesses divide'; 10:194-195 'The second reading rests'; 10:197 'the first reading grants his premise'; 10:213 'The witnesses refuse both'; 10:265 'on this reading'; 10:286 'The first reading hears'; 10:350 'The third reading draws'; 10:354 'the reading puts the two together'; 10:367-368 'The Communion's psalm carries ... the witnesses' readings of the flood'; 10:395 'Each reading hears ... in its own key'; 10:403 'The three readings'; 10:410 'contributes to all three readings'; 10:413 'the first reading hears'; 03-date-location.tex:25 'its second verse, Apoc 19:16, has no row' (the table's own mechanics in reader prose). (Hilary's 'grammar of the verse' at 10:329 is literal grammar and is not part of this finding.)
findings.required_result: Use the reader's words: 'the Mass', 'the texts', 'the Collect', 'this interpretation', 'the first interpretation', or the Father's name. Define the three interpretations once and refer to them plainly. Rewrites: 10:12-14 'The formulary can be read whole in three ways. The first, the Lamb who receives the kingdom, reads the Mass from the Introit and the Offertory.' -> 'The Mass as a whole can be interpreted in three ways. The first, the Lamb who receives the kingdom, starts from the Introit and the Offertory.' 10:90 'St Bede brings the same grammar to the Apocalypse itself.' -> 'St Bede reads the Apocalypse in the same way.' 10:185 'So the first and second readings differ at the Gospel ...' -> 'So the first and second interpretations differ at the Gospel ...'. 10:367-368 'The Communion's psalm carries, in the verse the antiphon cuts, the flood ..., and the witnesses' readings of the flood place ...' -> 'The verse of the psalm that the antiphon leaves out speaks of the flood ..., and the Fathers who explain the flood place ...'. synthesis.tex:21 '... three readings compared' -> '... three interpretations compared'. 03:25 '... its second verse, Apoc 19:16, has no row.' -> '... its second verse is Apoc 19:16.' (or leave the omission to the apparatus).

findings.problem: Phrases and theses return from section to section as refrains, and the closing comparison argues each section a second time instead of comparing them. Instances: 'in one sentence' for the Preface at 04-themes.tex:105 and again at 10-commentary.tex:435; 'the Lamb ... worthy ... because he was slain' at 04:24-25, 10:35-36 and 10:414; the straw 'territory' at 10:53 and 10:404; the three questions and each Father's answer, stated at 04:126-140 and stated again at 10:12-19 before the commentary develops them; 10:430-438, a closing paragraph that re-argues each interpretation ('The first, alone ... The second, alone ... The third, alone ...') and ends by restating the Preface quoted at 04:110-112.
findings.required_result: Say each thing once. Keep the three-question statement in one place, either the end of pages 3-4 or the start of the commentary. Let the closing subsection compare the four senses, which is its required job (10:412-428), and drop the refrain. Rewrites: 10:12-19: cut down to the sentence that is new, i.e. the verses where the witnesses disagree: 'The Fathers disagree on particular verses: the decree of the second psalm, the birth of Jn 18:37, the Son's subjection to the Father, and the moment when the Lord sits King for ever.' 10:434-438 'Together they say what the Preface says in one sentence: the anointed Son reigns by right, ...' -> cut; the Preface is quoted and discussed at 04:105-114 and 10:295-304. 10:35-36 '..., who is worthy to receive because he was slain.' -> end the sentence at 'their answers apply to the Introit's Lamb.'

findings.problem: Isolated cases of emphasis performed rather than earned: a rhetorical question closes a paragraph and is not worked out there (04-themes.tex:28 'Of the eternal Son, what can be received?', taken up only at 04:127-128 and on page 5); intensive 'itself' (04:24 'divinity itself'; 10-commentary.tex:90 'the Apocalypse itself'); a staged flourish (10:147 'Then he gives the answer its widest audience'); 10:405 'The cross has a place in each, and a different one.'
findings.required_result: Move the question to where the paragraph works it out, or state it as the difficulty (as 10:23-26 already does: 'The difficulty lies in two verbs'), and drop 04:28. Drop the intensive 'itself'. 10:147 -> 'Then Augustine addresses all kingdoms of the earth:'. 10:405 -> 'Each places the cross differently.'

findings.problem: Register leaks into the apparatus. Precise terms are allowed there, but 'the one join between two elements he makes himself', 'Every other connection drawn between elements belongs to the readings' and 'none of them carries a reading' are production jargon, not precise terms.
findings.required_result: E.g. 'Schuster treats the texts one by one and links only the Gradual and the Alleluia; every other link between texts is this study's, unless a Father is named as making it.' and 'none of them is the principal source of an interpretation.'
